concerns.concern: The paper never compares the composites' power factor with conventional devices. A rough estimate suggests the composite power factor (~5×10⁻¹³ W/mK²) is comparable to, not better than, the best thin-film devices, because S_SSE is about an order of magnitude lower. The claims of improved heat-to-electricity conversion are therefore not demonstrated.
concerns.quote: Without this comparison, statements such as 'enhancing the overall heat-to-electricity conversion capability' ... are not demonstrated by the data.

concerns.concern: The claim that the signal is purely SSE lacks a nonmagnetic control: an identically processed Pt-coated YAG or GGG composite. Such a control would bound ordinary Nernst, geometric and thermocouple artifacts. The ISHE sign check is also not discussed.
concerns.quote: the strongest and most standard test is missing: an identically processed Pt-coated nonmagnetic garnet (YAG or GGG) powder composite

concerns.concern: The isotropy evidence compares two configurations measured with different thermal setups (sapphire with grease vs Cu with tape), so the close agreement may be coincidental. How ∇_zT was determined is not described.
concerns.quote: The close numerical agreement may therefore be partly coincidental.

concerns.concern: The pressing axis relative to the x/z measurement axes is not stated. Uniaxial pressing typically causes texture, so it is unclear whether isotropy relative to the processing direction was actually tested.
concerns.quote: The paper does not state how x and z relate to the pressing axis

concerns.concern: The Hall test and all rotated-configuration data come from a single sample (30-RT) from a single batch.
concerns.quote: The Hall test and all rotated-configuration data also come from a single sample (30-RT) from a single batch.

concerns.concern: The '2–3 orders of magnitude' σ^eff improvement is overstated: the lowest composite is only ~10× the best conventional device, so 1–3 orders is fair.
concerns.quote: A fair statement is 1–3 orders.

concerns.concern: The claim that composite conductivities exceed oxide-based bulk ANE materials is overstated, since the 15-nm samples fall within that range rather than above it.
concerns.quote: 15-RT (5.6×10²) and 15-300 (8.4×10²) fall within that range, not above it.

concerns.concern: The Pt-dilution argument against ferromagnetic secondary phases is weak, because a ~1 wt% Fe₃O₄/FePt phase would be masked by the dilution. No upper bound on such a phase fraction is given.
concerns.quote: the argument that Pt dilution lowers M_s, so no FM phase exists, is weak.

concerns.concern: All four samples show a similar ~25% M_s reduction despite a 2× difference in Pt thickness. This is not obviously consistent with simple Pt mass dilution and is not explained.
concerns.quote: All four samples show a similar ~25% reduction even though the Pt thickness differs by 2×.

concerns.concern: The quoted YIG magnetization (37.9 emu/g) is the ~0 K value, while the comparison values for iron oxides are room-temperature values. The room-temperature value of YIG is ~27 emu/g.
concerns.quote: 37.9 emu/g corresponds to the ~0 K moment of YIG

concerns.concern: The magnetization axes in Fig. 3f and Fig. S6 (~0.02–0.027 'emu/g') are three orders of magnitude below the stated values and appear mislabeled.
concerns.quote: That is three orders of magnitude below either number, so the axis is presumably mislabeled

concerns.concern: XRD cannot cleanly exclude Fe₃O₄ or FePt: their main peaks overlap with YIG and broad Pt reflections, and lab XRD has a percent-level detection limit. The admitted inability to distinguish α-Fe₂O₃/YFeO₃ also conflicts with the strong exclusion statement.
concerns.quote: Percent-level impurities would therefore be hard to detect, and lab XRD typically has a detection limit of a few percent anyway.

concerns.concern: The same reference card number (PDF#43-0661) is assigned to both Y₂O₃ and FePt, so at least one phase is misidentified.
concerns.quote: both Y₂O₃ and FePt are labeled with the same card 'PDF#43-0661'

concerns.concern: The YIG powder size and batch mass are not reported, so the Pt shell thickness cannot be checked. The 15 and 30 nm values are extrapolated from a single 5 nm/1 h TEM calibration.
concerns.quote: neither powder size distribution nor loaded powder mass is reported

concerns.concern: The Pt content and volume fraction are not measured or reported, although they determine σ^eff and the expected M_s dilution.
concerns.quote: The Pt volume fraction determines σ^eff and the expected M_s dilution.

concerns.concern: Relative densities are computed against pure YIG, ignoring the Pt content, which likely overstates the true relative density.
concerns.quote: Relative densities (67–75%) are computed against pure YIG (5.11 g/cm³).

concerns.concern: The sample dimensions used for the σ^eff and SSE measurements are not given.
concerns.quote: The σ^eff measurement geometry (L_x, L_y, t_D of the pellet pieces) is also not given.

concerns.concern: The S_SSE drop from 15 to 30 nm Pt is only ~15–20%, whereas thin-film theory predicts about a halving. Calling the trend consistent therefore offers little support for the SSE assignment.
concerns.quote: Calling the trend 'consistent' therefore offers little support for the SSE assignment.

concerns.concern: The sintering-temperature effect on S_SSE (~2×) is larger than the thickness effect and is not explained.
concerns.quote: The sintering-temperature effect (~2×) is larger than the thickness effect and is not explained.

concerns.concern: E_y(H) saturates at higher fields (≳2.5–5 kOe) than M(H) (~1 kOe). This mismatch is not discussed or demagnetization-corrected, and it could indicate additional contributions.
concerns.quote: A field-shape mismatch between E_y and M is also a classic indicator of additional contributions.

concerns.concern: The key isotropy sentence labels the earlier comparison configuration incorrectly, so as written it compares H_x-∇_zT with itself.
concerns.quote: as written the sentence compares the configuration with itself

concerns.concern: Calling the composites 'bad metals' is misleading: their conductivity comes from a diluted, porous Pt network, not from an intrinsic electronic regime.
concerns.quote: Borrowing this term implies an intrinsic electronic regime the data do not address.

concerns.concern: 'Robust mechanical integrity' is asserted without hardness, strength or thermal-cycling data, despite 25–33% porosity.
concerns.quote: With 25–33% porosity and cold-pressed bonding, 'robust' is not established.

concerns.concern: The Cu-Kα wavelength is inconsistent between Methods (0.15406 nm) and Note S2 (0.15418 nm).
concerns.quote: Methods give 0.15406 nm (Cu-Kα1), while Note S2 gives 0.15418 nm (weighted Kα).

concerns.concern: Note S2 refers to the XRD data as Fig. S2, but the XRD figure is Fig. S3.
concerns.quote: Note S2 also repeatedly refers to the XRD data as 'Fig. S2a/S2b', whereas the XRD figure is Fig. S3
